selected_evidence.requirement: sudo commands are logged with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
selected_evidence.summary: sudoers.d/sudo-logfile created and validated with visudo -c; log file created with 600 perms; test sudo commands by root and a test user recorded with timestamp, host, user, and command in /var/log/sudo-commands.log

selected_evidence.requirement: sudo log entries are kept out of the general system log
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline showed sudo previously wrote to /var/log/secure via authpriv syslog; after adding 'Defaults !syslog', /var/log/secure line count stayed identical (14->14, and 34->34 post-reboot) across sudo invocations, proving no new general-log entries were produced
Captured pre-restart boot_id, uptime, sudoers.d config contents, visudo validation, and log file permissions as the healthy baseline

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returns before disconnection
selected_evidence.summary: systemctl reboot scheduled via a detached background wrapper; command acknowledged successfully before the node went offline

selected_evidence.requirement: proof node1 actually restarted (changed boot identity)
selected_evidence.summary: Connection timed out while node1 was rebooting; exec became available again shortly after; boot_id changed from f54d7366-0403-4b05-93bb-b5c0a1818892 to 2cdef81a-e59d-4bf7-bb37-a735057f1ec9, with a fresh uptime-since timestamp, proving an actual restart

selected_evidence.requirement: post-restart recovery of sudo logging configuration and data
selected_evidence.summary: After restart, sudoers.d/sudo-logfile persisted and revalidated with visudo -c, log file permissions intact, and a fresh sudo command was correctly captured in /var/log/sudo-commands.log while /var/log/secure remained unaffected

cat > /etc/sudoers.d/sudo-logfile <<'EOF'
Defaults !syslog
Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log"
Defaults log_host, log_year, log_input, log_output
EOF
chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/sudo-logfile
visudo -c

touch /var/log/sudo-commands.log
chown root:root /var/log/sudo-commands.log
chmod 600 /var/log/sudo-commands.log
ls -la /var/log/sudo-commands.log
wc -l /var/log/secure
